cells.tense: The private cost and the public thanks are standing together in the room right now.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Give steady attention this week to whatever you set aside to get where you're going, the way you'd look after anything you mean to keep. Tell no one.
cells.core:
You're pointed at something bright, and nobody had to argue you into it. The weeks you spent on it are showing up outside you now — people say the word for it, and the word lands true. This is the shape of it going well: effort you made quietly is standing where it can be seen, and you didn't rig it.

Keep your hand on what you're growing. Go back to whatever you went without for this — a night, an offer, a quieter month — and spend a little attention on it through the week, the way you'd mind a plant you actually mean to keep. Keep that to yourself. Feeding it tells you what to hand the same care to next.
cells.sheetLine: What you gave up quietly is standing where others can see it.
cells.verb: set what was carried quietly where others can see it was carried
cells.place: on the road you already walk toward what you want, before anyone confirms you chose right

cells.tense: You'll be bracing for the thanks that finally arrive and don't land right.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: This week, tell apart the wish to be thanked and the honest worth of the work itself, and feed only the second one.
cells.core:
You're already at the parade in your head — who will say what, whether the applause will land right, whether the thing you gave up will finally get its name read. Anticipating it has gotten heavier than the work it's aimed at. Nobody has thanked you yet for what isn't finished, and waiting is costing you the present.

Practice telling the two apart. Sit with wanting to be seen and the plain worth of the thing itself, and notice which you keep feeding. Set them side by side on paper, one line each, and check which is getting the hours. Then do the work with that line folded away. Wanting to be seen can stay. What it's allowed to steer is what you shrink.

cells.tense: You kept the lamp under a basket long after the room had emptied.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Pick the hardest part of what you're after and carry it end to end without asking anyone to hold it, soften it, or check on you.
cells.core:
The direction you steer by still points somewhere, but you stopped walking toward it in daylight. What you gave up for it hasn't been put in front of anyone in a long time — you keep it inside, half-finished, where no one can weigh it. Answering to an audience isn't the point; it's that nothing you've been carrying has anywhere to land, so it stays carried.

Start by holding what's already yours. Take the part of that pursuit which needs no permission, and see it through without handing any weight to someone else to check. When it's finished, something is on the table that's yours and visible to you. The others can come back after that.

cells.tense: The honoring is already happening through your hands and you have filed it as coincidence.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Stay beside something you keep going without being asked, long enough to see it's your own upkeep that holds it. Keep that recognition to yourself.
cells.core:
The thanks that makes this complete is being handed out, in small ways, all around you — and the hand passing it is yours. You hold people, projects, the thing that keeps the group upright, and when asked you'd say it just happens. The work is real and it has arrived. What's missing is any sense that you're the source of it.

Go back to the plainest version. Take a person you check on, a thing you maintain with nobody asking, and stay with it long enough to own that you're doing the maintaining. Nothing changes about the work. What changes is who holds the pen when you look at it.

attempts.check: The draftiest move would be to say the person has 'been denied credit' — the record only says the honor is external and now visible, not that any particular public ever withheld it, so nothing about their history or who failed to see them may be said. A reader could reasonably say 'I don't do this for the parade' — and the ask survives that, because it never requires an audience, only the person's own hand on what they keep lit. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about 'waiting to be seen' as a condition; cut it and let the wanting be first.
